newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge up, focus on Welteke comments.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge up, focus on Welteke comments.

text.p: Irish bonds edged up in thin late trade on Friday but underperformed German bunds as comments by Bundesbank board member Ernst Welteke proved the main story of the day, dealers said.
"The market is finishing a bit stronger but has been a major underperformer," one dealer said. "The main focus of the day was the comments by Welteke."
Welteke's comments soothed some concerns on the instability of a post-EMU euro currency when he suggested that there should be a core of strong countries at the start of EMU.
But he did not see Ireland in the first wave of countries participating in EMU.
He said capital markets were already pointing to an inner core of European Union countries which would be able to take part in European monetary union from the beginning.

"If you look at the convergence of interest rates, the capital markets have already decided which states will join at the start - Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Germany, France and Austria," Welteke told a Moscow news conference on Friday.
He said Ireland, Denmark and Finland would be the next candidates to join.

By 1700 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up five pence from Thursday's close at 102.60 to yield 5.76 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 10 pence at 109.45 to yield 6.51 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 93 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 160 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area.
